Let
\[
L=\log2,\qquad M=\log\frac32,\qquad r=2L-3M,
\]
and for \(s>0\) small set
\[
\alpha=(2-4Ls)^p,\qquad \beta=(4-(8L-12M)s)^p=(4(1-rs))^p .
\]
The only distances which change from \(s=0\) are
\[
d_s(a_1,a_3)=d_s(b_1,b_3)=2-4Ls,\qquad d_s(a_2,b_2)=4-(8L-12M)s.
\]

For a coefficient vector \(c\) with \(\sum c_z=0\), write
\[
Q_{p,s}(c)=\sum_{z,w}c_zc_wd_s(z,w)^p.
\]
By the symmetries \(a_1\leftrightarrow a_3\), \(b_1\leftrightarrow b_3\), and \(a\leftrightarrow b\), the zero-sum space splits into small blocks.

The endpoint-flip blocks give \(Q=-2\alpha t^2<0\), so they never determine the critical exponent. The important antisymmetric arm block has coefficients
\[
c_{a_1}=c_{a_3}=x,\quad c_{a_2}=y,\quad
c_{b_1}=c_{b_3}=-x,\quad c_{b_2}=-y,\quad c_\ast=0.
\]
For this block,
\[
Q_{p,s}=
\begin{pmatrix}x&y\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
4\alpha-8\cdot2^p & 4(1-3^p)\\
4(1-3^p) & -2\beta
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus the boundary is given by
\[
\Delta_-(p,s)
=(4\alpha-8\cdot2^p)(-2\beta)-16(1-3^p)^2=0.
\]

At \(s=0\),
\[
\Delta_-(p,0)=8\cdot8^p-16(3^p-1)^2.
\]
This vanishes at \(p=1\), and for \(p>1\),
\[
\frac{3^p-1}{2^{(3p-1)/2}}
\]
is increasing from \(1\), so \(\Delta_-(p,0)<0\). Meanwhile \((Y,d_0)\) embeds into \(\ell_1^4\) via
\[
\ast=0,\quad a_1=e_1,\quad a_3=e_2,\quad a_2=e_1+e_2,\quad
b_1=e_3,\quad b_3=e_4,\quad b_2=e_3+e_4,
\]
so it has \(p\)-negative type for every \(0<p\le1\). Hence
\[
\wp(0)=1.
\]

Now put
\[
p=1+x,\qquad x=x(s).
\]
Using
\[
(1-2Ls)^p=1-2Ls-2Lxs+O(s^3),
\]
\[
(1-rs)^p=1-rs-rxs+O(s^3),
\]
one obtains
\[
\frac{\Delta_-(p,s)}8
=24M(s-x)
+\bigl(24M-26L^2+60LM-30M^2\bigr)s^2
+O(s^3)
\]
when \(x=s+O(s^2)\). Therefore if
\[
x=s+cs^2+O(s^3),
\]
then \(\Delta_-(p,s)=0\) gives
\[
c=\frac{24M-26L^2+60LM-30M^2}{24M}.
\]
So the antisymmetric obstruction gives
\[
\wp(s)=1+s+\frac{24M-26L^2+60LM-30M^2}{24M}s^2+O(s^3).
\]

The symmetric arm block also has a zero eigenvalue at \((p,s)=(1,0)\), but its corresponding second-order coefficient is larger, so it is not the first obstruction for \(s>0\) small. Hence the above branch determines \(\wp(s)\).

Thus
\[
\wp'(0^+)=1,
\]
and
\[
\wp''(0^+)=
\frac{24M-26L^2+60LM-30M^2}{12M}.
\]

\[
\boxed{
\left(
1,\,
1,\,
\frac{24\log\frac32-26(\log2)^2+60(\log2)(\log\frac32)-30(\log\frac32)^2}{12\log\frac32}
\right)
}
\]
